task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: primary play types of absent player
methodological_questions: Can the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types be identified from pre-absence initiation profile similarity, minutes, or same-position minutes?
How many absence spells are needed to test teammate redistribution with play-type data?
Which measures of play-type gain are reliable across seasons, and which confounders (minutes, lineup, injury severity) threaten inference?
evidence_establishes: No earlier study-family record was returned by retrieve_history, so no prior finding for this question is established by the tool.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the closest-profile teammate, the highest-minutes teammate, or the same-position teammate is the largest gainer.
Whether any prior project result on play-type redistribution exists, supports, or contradicts the hypothesis.
Whether the 148 spells are usable as independent tests, given they are nested within 11 cases.
own_inferences: The prediction has three alternative operationalisations (closest profile, most minutes/initiations, same-position minutes) joined by 'or'. As posed, it is not a single testable claim.
With 11 absent-player cases, a top-1 'largest gainer' hit rate has very few trials. Chance performance depends on roster size, so the baseline must be computed per case, not assumed.
Spells within one absence case share the same absent player, team and season, so they are not independent. The effective sample is closer to 11 cases than 148 spells.
Derived play-type labels and initiator attribution come from a graph built on play-by-play. Their error rates are unknown and may differ by player role, so the gain measure inherits label error.
uncertainties: Definition of 'primary types' and 'gain' (absolute change in initiations, share change, or points per possession) is not specified.
Pre-absence window length and minimum-minutes thresholds are not specified.

The 2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13, and the 2025-26 playoffs only from 2026-06-21. Any data pulled on 2026-11-01 from those seasons is therefore partial or complete depending on the file, so the data version must be fixed.
Injury severity and reason for absence are not in the data catalogue, so they cannot be controlled.
Number of eligible teammates per case is unknown and determines the chance baseline.

historical_effect.explanation: retrieve_history returned zero records, so no earlier result could inform the decision. The decision rests on the design constraints in the task itself: 11 effective cases, three competing predictors, and an undefined gain measure.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 absence cases are available. A top-1 gainer test across these cases has very low power to distinguish the three predictors from chance.
Spells per absent player are few and unevenly distributed across play types, so the primary-type gain estimates for each case may rest on small counts.
Three predictors and several gain definitions produce many candidate comparisons; testing all of them against the same cases inflates false positives.
Play-type initiator labels are derived from play-by-play, so the gain outcome is itself a derived label whose error is unmeasured.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it cannot be determined whether this question has already been answered. The status is recorded as unknown, not as no.

risks.text: Eleven cases give a very small number of top-1 trials. Chance hit rates depend on roster size and could be near the observed value by luck.
Few initiations per teammate in the pre- and post-absence windows make profile similarity and gain estimates unstable.
Initiation profiles and gain measures may not be stable across seasons. Reliability of the play-type labels is unknown.
Absences are often selected after a slump or injury, so pre-absence profiles and post-absence gains may reflect regression to the mean rather than redistribution.
The gain outcome depends on derived initiator and play-type labels, so label error propagates directly into the outcome.
Initiator attribution in play-by-play may be misassigned for assisted or team-action plays, biasing gains for particular teammates.
Minutes, lineup changes, coaching changes, and injury severity can each drive both teammate gains and the chosen predictor, and none is controlled in the stated data.
The 'or' across three predictors and unspecified gain definitions creates a garden of forking paths.
The chance that any single teammate is the largest gainer depends on roster size, which varies by case and has not been computed.
Seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 differ in rules, pace and roster context, and the 2025-26 files are partial or complete depending on the date pulled.
No placebo or null-absence comparison is defined, so a 'largest gainer' pattern cannot be distinguished from a general tendency for high-usage players to absorb usage.
Joining play-by-play, substitution intervals and derived possession records across per-game files can misalign spells and players, which would bias the cases.

design.estimand: For each absence case, whether one pre-specified teammate (chosen by one pre-specified rule) has the largest change in initiations in the absent player's primary play types, compared with the chance rate for that case's roster.
design.unit: Absence case (absent player x team x season), with spells nested within cases. Spells are not treated as independent units.
design.sample: The 11 cases, as listed. Spell-level data are used only inside cases. Minimum-minutes and minimum-initiation thresholds are fixed before analysis.
design.power: Not achievable at useful power with 11 cases. The minimum viable test is a case-level sign or rank test against a per-case permutation baseline. This is descriptive unless the case count is increased.
design.controls: Pre-absence minutes, lineup stability, and play-type base rates for each teammate. Injury severity is not available and is stated as an uncontrolled confounder. Use pre-absence-only windows for the predictor, and post-absence-only windows for the gain, to avoid leakage.
design.falsification: A placebo analysis that applies the same rule to periods without absence, and to a randomly chosen non-absent player's play types. If the placebo shows the same top-gainer pattern, the result is an artifact of usage redistribution in general.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one predictor (closest profile by a single named distance), one gain measure, and one primary play-type definition. Report the other two predictors and other gain definitions as secondary, with correction.
design.decision_rule: Treat the question as not testable as posed. If the revised design is run, report the case-level hit rate against the per-case permutation baseline with an exact or permutation p-value, and state explicitly that no population-level claim follows from 11 cases.
design.data_version: Lock the NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular-season and playoff files at a fixed pull date. Record the 2025-26 completion status (regular season complete from 2026-04-13; playoffs complete from 2026-06-21) and exclude any partial files.
